get.summary: Liveness: is this process still capable of doing work at all?
get.description:
Fails only when a worker this process started has exited, which is
unrecoverable in-process: the HTTP server would go on accepting
submissions that nothing will ever consume. Deliberately does no I/O, so a
store outage does not answer this question; otherwise a single database
blip would restart every instance at once and turn a degradation into an
outage.

The contract is the status code. Wiring it to a container health check, a
process supervisor or a periodic request is a deployment decision.

200.description: Process is live and its workers are running

503.description: A worker has exited; this instance cannot process work

get.summary: Readiness: should this instance be given more work right now?
get.description:
Unlike liveness this may touch the job store, because an instance that
cannot reach it can only fail whatever it accepts. A failure here is
expected to be transient and must not cause the instance to be replaced.

ApiAssertionDef.description:
A single custom assertion to embed in the C2PA manifest.

Only JSON payloads are accepted at this endpoint. Use a reverse-domain label
(`com.example.label`) to avoid collisions with standard C2PA assertions.

data.description: Arbitrary JSON payload embedded in the manifest assertion.

ApiInputRef.description:
Where to read an input file or folder from.

`RemoteFileUrl`/`RemoteFolderUrl` cover both HTTP(S) and S3 sources: the
scheme of `url` (`https://` vs `s3://`) selects the resolver at request
time, there is no separate variant per provider. HTTP has no request-level
auth mechanism; use a presigned URL to grant scoped, temporary access. S3
access (credentials, allowed buckets) is configured server-side and never
appears in the request body.

Note: an in-request (multipart) upload variant is intentionally not
documented here yet, since no `/v2` endpoint can currently accept one.

ApiOutputSpec.description:
Output specification for API requests.

The `output` section selects the destination and placement: `prefix` is an
optional caller namespace and `name` an optional logical output folder/base;
each input contributes its own leaf. The file-leaf naming convention is
configured per output sink in the service config, not per request. Omitting
`output` is equivalent to `local` with no fields.

This is pure request data and is always available; whether an `s3` destination
can actually be served is a deployment concern (the `s3` build feature and the
configured bucket allow-list), resolved by the output sink factory and rejected
by request validation when unavailable.

oneOf.description: Opaque reference token (no file resolved; bare ingredient).
Actual media file whose C2PA manifest is read and included in the chain.

ApiParent.description: Global or per-input parent manifest source.

oneOf.description:
A file inside the input folder this job is already processing,
addressed by its path relative to that folder's root
(`"1/init_1.mp4"`, `"mezzanine.mov"`).

Nothing is fetched: a folder input is downloaded in full before signing
starts, so any file in it can act as the parent, including one the
media scanner does not pick up for signing. The path is resolved per
input, against *that* input's folder.

**Supported by `/v2/c2pa/package` and `/v2/sync/c2pa/package` only.**
The other signing endpoints reject it; extending them is tracked as
issue #181.

ApiParentFileSource.description:
Where the media file behind a file-based parent comes from.

The first two are locators the service fetches on its own. The third is
not a locator at all: it names a file the caller has already sent as part
of this job.

oneOf.description: None = disable parent for this input.

assertions.description: Optional custom assertions to embed in the C2PA manifest.

oneOf.description: Optional parent manifest to attach as a provenance ingredient.

parent_overrides.description: Per-input overrides for the parent manifest.

C2paAudioRequest.description:
Request for the C2PA audio signing endpoint.

Inputs must be single files whose extension names a container the C2PA SDK
can sign: `mp3`, `wav`, `flac`, `m4a`, and `mp4`/`m4v` for audio-only
assets. An input with no derivable extension is accepted and its media type
is settled during resolution.

assertions.description: Optional custom assertions to embed in the C2PA manifest.

oneOf.description: Optional parent manifest to attach as a provenance ingredient.

parent_overrides.description: Per-input overrides for the parent manifest.

Optional parent manifest to attach as a provenance ingredient.

This is the only endpoint that also accepts an `input_relative_path`
parent source, naming a file inside the input folder it is already
packaging (see `ApiParentFileSource`).

JobResultResponse.description: Complete job result response (for sync endpoints and status queries)

PackageParams.description:
Parameters for media packaging.

The output destination and name are set in the request `output` section.
This type has no fields and keeps the request schema shape stable.

ProcessingResult.description: Result for a single input in a job

bearer.description:
Access token (a JWT) issued by the deployment's OpenID Connect provider, normally to a machine client through the OAuth 2.0 client credentials grant. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

Every operation except the health and readiness probes needs a token. The submit and run operations also list the scope they need, and a token without it gets 403: `c2pa:sign` (submit C2PA signing jobs, including package and sign) or `c2pa:package` (submit packaging-only jobs). `c2pa:jobs:read:all` lets a client read any job; without it a client reads only the jobs it submitted, and another client's job answers 404 like an unknown id.

Only builds with the `oidc` feature enforce this; a build without it accepts every request.
